hypotheses.justification: The proof uses hB only to call reducedTermEval1632 and reducedTermEval1633. Each of those uses it only to call sound4547 / sound4548 (MixedSemantics/Sound71.lean). There it is the unused binder `_hB`: the proof is `have hc : mixedVector B (Sum.inr 4547) = mixedMoment B node4547 node4547Labels := rfl; simpa [nodeValue4547, Sparse.eval] using hc.symm`, and it does not involve hB. The other lemmas in the chain (reducedMerge1625Check, which is proved by `decide`; reducedTermArithmetic1632/1633, which hold for any `x : Master → ℝ`; Integer.Sparse.eval_mergeBy; Integer.Sparse.eval_append) take no MUB hypothesis. So the identity holds for every B. A proof without hB inlines the rfl/simpa step instead of calling sound4547/4548, then runs the same `rw [reducedTermArithmetic163x]`, `change` and `ring` steps. hF can be deleted as well, independently or together with hB.

Same chain as for hB: hF reaches only sound4547 and sound4548, where it is the unused binder `_hF`. Those proofs are `rfl` on the definition of mixedVector plus `simpa` unfolding nodeValue4547/4548 and Sparse.eval. All the other lemmas used (reducedMerge1625Check, reducedTermArithmetic1632/1633, Integer.Sparse.eval_mergeBy, Integer.Sparse.eval_append) are pure arithmetic or decidable facts with no Fourier hypothesis. So the statement holds for every B, and the proof goes through by inlining the rfl/simpa argument. hB can be deleted as well, independently or together with hF.
